bullets: Sunspots: cooler dark magnetic patches; 11-year cycle - matched by plasma currents in the 35,000-km-deep Near-Surface Shear Layer (LENS, May 2025).

Flares/CMEs hit satellites, GPS, aviation, radio, power grids; cause auroras . Aditya-L1 showed the Oct 2024 storm strongly compressed Earth's magnetic shield (TH, 11 Jan 2026). ESA-China SMILE (Vega-C) will image the solar wind-magnetosphere link (LENS, Apr 2026).

Solar flares: sudden bursts of radiation from magnetic reconnection, classed A, B, C, M, X (X strongest). CMEs: plasma clouds from the corona at 250-3,000 km/s, reaching Earth in 1-3 days.
Effects on Earth: geomagnetic storms, auroras, damage to satellites, communication, navigation and power grids.

bullets: Extends from about 60 km to over 1,000 km. Solar UV and X-rays strip electrons from atoms; charged particles cause auroras and airglow; it reflects radio waves back to Earth, which allows long-distance communication. F (Appleton; F1, F2 by day): Height ~150 km upward; Role Main reflector of short-wave radio
Within the thermosphere, about 80-400 km; electrically charged ions reflect radio waves transmitted from Earth, making long-distance radio possible.
F (Appleton; F1, F2): Height ~150-400 km; Note Reflects short waves; key for long-distance radio
